title: The Day the Cabin Hogged the Blankets
skyStory: The moon has slipped into Cancer, its own home sign, ninety-four percent lit and very happy to be back. Cancer moons nest. They pile up quilts, light the lamps early and insist everyone take their shoes off. Outside, the late November dark arrives before supper. Inside, every hearth glows a little brighter, as if the moon whispered a reminder to all of them at once.

reading: The cabin is in full nesting mode today. Every blanket in the place has migrated to one couch and the woodstove is crackling like it is telling stories. The Tiger may grumble about too much coziness. It will lose.

Home is the assignment. Fix one small thing that has bugged you for months: the squeaky hinge, the drawer that sticks, the lamp that flickers. Then sit near the thing you fixed and admire it unreasonably. Someone will come by or call, and the right move is to let them make you the warm drink. The [[Ten of Cups]] is drawing a rainbow over the roofline and would like you to look up.
joel.mission: Oil one squeaky hinge, or fix one tiny thing, and give it a small round of applause.
joel.omen: Smoke rising straight up from a chimney on a still evening. All is well at home base.

reading: The tide comes up to the edge of the woods today and stops politely, like a guest wiping its feet. Cancer is a water sign and it wants you to feel at home in yourself, not just in your house.

Make one corner of your space a little more yours. A photo on the wall. A shell on the sill. A candle that smells like the forest after rain. When you sit there tonight, tell the room a story about where that object came from. The room has been waiting for a good storyteller. Everything else can wait until morning, and it will, grumbling quietly in the hallway.
nancy.mission: Put one small object you love somewhere you will see it first thing tomorrow morning.
nancy.omen: A crab, a shell or a picture of the sea in an unexpected place. Home is following you around.

together.text: Each of you send a photo of the coziest corner you have right now. No staging allowed, real clutter and all. Rate each other's corner out of eleven, with one bonus point for a blanket and two for a sleeping animal.

game.intro: The cabin is hogging every blanket in the building, so the facts froze solid. Thaw something wrong for Saturn.
game.question: Why do we pull blankets up over our feet even when the room is warm?
